core_obligations: Use that the Koszul complex of f_1 to f_r tensored with S equals the Koszul complex of the images of the f_i over S (proof lines 7351-7354).
Combine that with associativity of the tensor product to rewrite (K(f) tensor over R with M) tensor over R with S as K(phi(f)) tensor over S with N (proof lines 7354-7356).

Read off that the vanishing of the homology required in the hypothesis implies the vanishing required for the base changed sequence, in both the H_1-regular and the Koszul-regular version (proof lines 7356-7357).

The nearest public records are 340 (7359-7438, tag 062I, first Koszul homology regularity implies quasi-regularity) and 341 (8259-8332, tag 07CZ); public 340 begins two lines after this card's proof ends and is a different statement about equivalent regularity notions.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that both versions of Koszul regularity of a sequence of elements, the version relative to a module and the absolute one, survive base change along a flat ring map: if f_1 to f_r is M-H_1-regular or M-Koszul-regular over R and S is a flat R-algebra, then the images of the f_i are N-H_1-regular or N-Koszul-regular for N = M tensor over R with S (statement lines 7336-7347). The proof is eight lines (proof lines 7350-7357) and it is a two-step identification: the Koszul complex of the sequence over S is the base change of the Koszul complex over R, and this identity together with associativity of the tensor product rewrites (K(f) tensor M) tensor S as K(phi(f)) tensor N, which is exactly the complex whose homology has to vanish. What a reader has to check is the second identity, since the first is the definition of the base changed sequence; the author displays the conclusion of both steps and stops there.
